narrative.text: Figure 1 — a JSON Schema rendered as a class diagram, generated from the natural-language prompt quoted beside it. Four boxes: `root` holding `experiments: object[]`; an `experiments entry` with `metal_salt: metalSalt`, `ligand: ligand`, `creator`, `date`, `temperature`, `duration` and `product_purity: boolean`; and TWO separate leaf definitions, `metalSalt` and `ligand`, each carrying an identical `name`/`mass`/`inchi` triple. That duplication is the point of the figure — it is what the next prompt asks to be removed.

Figure 2 — the same schema after a natural-language modification request. The two identical leaf definitions of Figure 1 have collapsed into ONE `compound` class carrying `name`/`mass`/`inchi`, and both `metal_salt` and `ligand` on the `experiments entry` now refer to it. The pair Fig. 1 → Fig. 2 is the paper's demonstration that a refactor can be requested in prose and applied to a validated model.
